meaning: Supabase rejected the request because the access token your app sent is past its expiry time (1 hour by default). The user is not really logged out; the app just sent an old token instead of refreshing it.
causes: The app stores the access_token itself (e.g. in localStorage or state) and reuses it after it expires instead of letting supabase-js manage the session.
A second Supabase client was created with a hard-coded Authorization header, so auto-refresh never applies to it.
The browser tab slept (laptop lid closed) and a request fired before the refresh finished.
Server code (Edge Function, API route) is passed a token captured at login hours earlier.

steps.text: Create one Supabase client for the whole app and let it manage the session. Do not pass a fixed Authorization header.
Whenever you need a token (e.g. to call your own API), read it fresh right before the request instead of caching it.
steps.code:
const { data: { session } } = await supabase.auth.getSession()
await fetch('/api/thing', { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${session?.access_token}` } })

steps.text: Listen for auth changes so the UI updates when a refresh fails and the user really is signed out.
To call a Supabase Edge Function, use supabase.functions.invoke(), which attaches the current token for you.
Test it: in DevTools > Application > Local Storage, find the sb-...-auth-token entry, wait past expiry (or temporarily lower JWT expiry in Auth settings) and confirm requests still succeed.

prompt: My app gets 'JWT expired' errors from Supabase after the user has been logged in for about an hour. Make sure the whole app uses a single Supabase client created with autoRefreshToken: true and persistSession: true, remove any place where we store or hard-code the access_token, and read the token with supabase.auth.getSession() right before any fetch that needs it. Add an onAuthStateChange listener that sends the user to /login on SIGNED_OUT.

faq.q: Should I just increase the JWT expiry?
faq.a: You can, under Auth settings, but it only delays the error and makes stolen tokens valid longer. Fix the refresh instead.

faq.q: Why does it only happen sometimes?
faq.a: It only fails on requests made with a token older than the expiry time, typically after an hour of idling or a sleeping tab.
